channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Slovakia: PM Robert Fico's NATO Article 5 remarks spark criticism and raise questions about his country's NATO commitment
item.description: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico says he fears war and will do everything he can to keep his country out of one. Critics say his remarks risk weakening NATO, the alliance that was designed to prevent such a war.

item.title: [DW] Famine threatens the Ukrainian town of Oleshky in the southern Kherson region as Russia delays creating a humanitarian evacuation corridor
item.description: Food supplies to the town of Oleshky, in the occupied part of the southern Kherson region, have been cut off since May. Efforts by Kyiv to negotiate the evacuation of civilians with Moscow have been largely unsuccessful.

item.title: [DW] Military aircraft crashes near US air base in Spangdahlem, Germany
item.description: The F-16 pilot was able to safely eject from the plane and was taken to receive medical care. The incident occurred near Spangdahlem Air Base in the German state of Rhineland-Palatinate.

item.title: [DW] 'Swan Song': New book by Princess Diana's brother drops
item.description: A memoir penned by Charles Spencer on his older sister's life has been released, opening old royal wounds nearly three decades after Princess Diana's death.

item.title: [EU Observer] Deporting humans becomes big business, as Brussels and Washington race to pay African countries to take them
item.description: The Americans have secured some 35 deals to deport people, often with no strings attached. The multi-million US dollar business appears to have turned into a race with the Europeans, who are hoping to secure their first deal with the Rwandans.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU’s Costa calls out ‘dangerous escalation’ by Russia amid increasing hybrid attacks
item.description: Russia's hybrid attacks on Europe are "unacceptable," EU Council president António Costa said in New York, as threats increase across the continent.

item.title: [EU Observer] Mining firms’ plea for EU critical minerals budget falls on deaf ears
item.description: Mining companies want a dedicated EU budget for critical raw materials, citing ineffective EU financing and the risk of being pushed aside by other priorities. But the European Commission and member states prefer to keep the money flexible.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU data chief adds voice to unions’ fears of ‘carte blanche’ use of workers’ data for AI
item.description: EU data protection chief Wojciech Wiewiórowski has joined trade unions and privacy activists in their concerns over the ‘digital omnibus’, which includes amendments to EU privacy rules that would allow data harvesting from workers without their permission to feed AI models.

item.title: [EU Observer] Macron’s ego may just have permanently damaged EU unity on Russia
item.description: France has a history of non-compliance with EU rules, such as its years-long trampling on the Stability and Growth Pact, and is second only to Italy in the number of EU-law infringement cases it has fought in the European Court of Justice over the decades.

item.title: [EU Observer] Russians dream of encircling Dobropillia, as Ukraine’s Azov force pushes back (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,673)
item.description: While Kyiv suffers the highest number of Russian attacks since March 2022, Russian Z bloggers have exaggerated claims of trapping Ukrainian soldiers in "cauldrons” in Dobropillia.

item.title: [DW] Czech PM Andrej Babis reiterates importance of NATO for his country but rejects calls to increase defense spending
item.description: The US and NATO want Czechia to spend more on defense. Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis says Prague cannot afford faster increases, despite growing warnings about the threat from Russia.

item.title: [DW] 'Pope fever' takes hold as Pope Leo visits France
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is expected to draw huge crowds during his visit to France. As part of his trip, he's also set to address Europe's future and some of the challenges ahead.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU is drawing up membership action plans for most promising candidates
item.description: For the first time, Brussels is considering setting target dates for Montenegro, Ukraine, Moldova and Albania to complete key stages of accession talks.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Independent wins Kraków mayorship first round, as far right sees setback for Tusk
item.description: Łukasz Gibała and a candidate backed by PM Donald Tusk move on to a runoff as parties jostle ahead of a fall 2027 general election.

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump asked Xi if China wanted to buy American weapons, US envoy says
item.description: Administration denies delaying sale of a $14bn arms package to Taiwan to appease Beijing

item.title: [Politico Europe] Britain to keep tariffs on Chinese EVs ‘under review,’ UK business chief says
item.description: Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said the U.K.’s position on the issue was "finely balanced" as officials pursue talks with Brussels.

item.title: [Politico Europe] UK business minister warns potential US diesel export ban ‘significant concern’
item.description: The U.K. receives around one-sixth of its diesel from the U.S. and would be one of the countries most exposed to an export ban.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU rejoin push risks causing uncertainty, warns business secretary
item.description: Jonathan Reynolds said the focus should be on improving Britain's trading relationship with Brussels.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Bill Gates says an AI ‘kill switch’ isn’t enough
item.description: The Microsoft co-founder called for mandatory monitoring of powerful artificial intelligence systems in an NBC interview that aired Sunday.

item.title: [EU Observer] Chess body FIDE elects Kazakh billionaire, amid Russia’s return to world sports
item.description: The fact a Russia-linked billionaire was elected by 110 votes out of 192 in FIDE was a sad reminder that Putin still had friends outside Europe.

item.title: [Financial Times] Terrorism arrests made in ‘major incident’ near RAF Fairford
item.description: President Donald Trump suggests US worked with UK to prevent an attack on air base used for US strikes on Iran

item.title: [Politico Europe] Burnham must be ‘selective’ in conference speech, says key ally
item.description: Liverpool City Region Mayor Steve Rotheram, who has seen a draft of the PM's address, said there is "no way" he can cover all his arguments in one hour.

item.title: [Financial Times] Corporate America embraces cheaper ‘open’ AI models
item.description: US businesses far beyond Silicon Valley are adopting Chinese alternatives to OpenAI and Anthropic’s systems

item.title: [Financial Times] Pay to play in the age of corporate migration
item.description: States are feeling more pressure from companies demanding subsidies and tax breaks

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU Commission calls on countries to cut energy demands as costs surge
item.description: In a letter seen by POLITICO, Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen asked ministers to introduce new measures "in the context of constrained global supply."

item.title: [DW] European cities seek ways of boosting affordable housing
item.description: In many major urban centers of Europe, the housing shortage has become an explosive social issue. DW looks into various models that have been put in place across the continent.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Swiss say no to hardening neutrality principle, safeguarding sanctions on Russia
item.description: The Kremlin backed the referendum proposal, which was opposed by the Swiss government.

item.title: [Financial Times] The India shock: exporting workers to the world
item.description: Emigration has helped New Delhi manage its labour surplus, but the strategy has limits

item.title: [Politico Europe] Northern Ireland standoff puts peace and power-sharing at risk
item.description: A sudden revival of the 1990s confrontations between Orange Order marchers and Catholic demonstrators puts the police back in the middle — and leaders of Northern Ireland’s supposed unity government on opposite sides.

item.title: [Financial Times] Investors pursue Dubai investment group over missing payments
item.description: AIX accused of having skipped or delayed payouts on bond-like products offering double-digit annual returns

item.title: [EU Observer] Lithuania moves to lift ban on nuclear weapons as ‘Russians do not attack the strong’
item.description: Lithuania's parliament this week backed a proposal to lift the constitutional ban on the deployment of nuclear weapons and foreign military bases, opening the way for future deployment of nuclear weapons in the country.

item.title: [Financial Times] Private credit turmoil eases as investor withdrawals slow
item.description: ‘Too early to call the bottom’ but redemption requests from retail investors fall

item.title: [Financial Times] US housing crunch puts private equity in midterm campaign crosshairs
item.description: FT analysis shows that institutional investors are being blamed for soaring costs

item.title: [Financial Times] Big companies warn lack of ‘AI openness’ could hit investment in Europe
item.description: Multinationals evaluating countries’ approach to AI before making expansion plans, say executives

item.title: [DW] Backlash over data centers tests Europe's AI ambitions
item.description: Massive data centers needed to run AI are triggering protests across Europe. Their operators counter that they boost digital sovereignty and energy independence.

item.title: [DW] Russia expected to intensify hybrid war on Europe
item.description: Drone explosions, airspace violations, arson attacks: Poland, Romania, and Moldova are now regularly targeted in Russian attacks against Ukraine. More governments are calling these attacks deliberate acts of aggression.

item.title: [DW] Russian students: Propaganda in school prepares them to die
item.description: The Russian government wants children to learn about patriotism from an early age. DW spoke to students in Siberia about their views on propaganda at school on the war in Ukraine and their future.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘Poor but sexy’ Berlin faces worsening housing crisis and bad fixes, warns German economist
item.description: Over the last decade, Berlin rent has spiked 75 percent to €15.78 per square metre. Economist Alexander Kritikos breaks down the bureaucratic nightmare of building housing in the German capital and warned how the Left's plans to purchase flats from corporate landlords may not yield the desired results.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine steps up measures to protect railways
item.description: As Russia increases its attacks on Ukraine's rail infrastructure, the Ukrainian government has called for help to replace destroyed locomotives and is making plans to keep passengers safe.

item.title: [DW] Ever more Israelis moving to and investing in Cyprus
item.description: Over the past three years, more and more Israelis have been purchasing property and investing in Cyprus, with many moving to the island permanently. How has this changed the Cypriot economy and how are locals responding?

item.title: [DW] 'Lithuanian skies are NATO skies': DW speaks with Lithuanian premier Mindaugas Sinkevicius
item.description: In a DW interview, Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius discussed threats to Lithuania from Russia and Belarus, NATO's need for stronger air defense and why military spending alone cannot ensure security.

item.title: [EU Observer] First blind the Russians, then catch them with robots: Ukraine’s Operation Vivaldi shows cutting edge of modern warfare (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,674)
item.description: By driving Russian forces back to their 2022 lines and crippling refineries deep in Samara, Operation Vivaldi shows how a tech-heavy Ukrainian corps can threaten not just a single sector near Lyman, but Russia’s wider ability to wage war.

item.title: [EU Observer] Deadlock on EU pesticides bill after scientists call for pause
item.description: Amid pushback from the European scientific community and countries outside the bloc, EU officials are under pressure to suspend negotiations on a Food and Feed law.

item.title: [EU Observer] How a Chinese ‘smart sex toys’ company fed Russian war tech against Ukraine — and exposed an EU sanctions blind spot
item.description: Sanction one company, and another appears. Europe needs to start screening addresses in the EU sanctions-list against Russia. Most are in China and Hong Kong, but have generic names, no websites, and almost no public footprint.

item.title: [EU Observer] Shadow fleet tankers flock back to being flagged as Russian, creating more headaches for EU states
item.description: Tankers are re-flagging 'en masse' to Russia, in order to dodge EU crackdowns. So European governments now face the risk that a detained ship could trigger a more direct diplomatic clash with Moscow.

item.title: [DW] How Bulgaria become a global leader in battery storage and what this means for the country's grid and energy market?
item.description: In under two years, Bulgaria has become one of the world's most battery-intensive energy markets. Can the surge last — and what will it mean for conventional power generators?

item.title: [EU Observer] The pay gap isn’t dead, and Brussels is a hotbed for it – even in the NGO sector
item.description: The pay-gap 'myth' is alive and well, and these women are the proof. Since Brussels attempted to implement its EU Pay directive, their job terminations could have been avoidable. Member states like Belgium are yet to implement the change, where pay discrimination persists - even in the human rights sector.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: How do European authorities deal with misogynism online?
item.description: Misoginistic online networks are on the rise. How are countries dealing with this surge among young men?

item.title: [DW] Italy to ban burqa in schools, limit foreign pupils
item.description: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s government has passed new school rules capping the number of students who don't speak fluent Italian and banning face coverings.
